stem:
A technology magazine selected 150 smartphones of one particular model at random from a manufacturer's warehouse. For each phone, the magazine fully charged the battery and measured how many hours the phone played video before the battery ran out. The mean battery life for the sample was 11.2 hours, with an associated margin of error of 0.4 hours.

Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion based on these results?
explanation:
Choice C is correct. The sample was chosen at random from phones of this one model in the warehouse, so the result applies to that population. The estimate plus or minus the margin of error gives a plausible range for the population mean: $11.2 - 0.4 = 10.8$ and $11.2 + 0.4 = 11.6$ hours.

Choice A is incorrect. The sample mean is an estimate, not the exact population mean.

Choice B is incorrect. Only one model was sampled, so the result can't be applied to every model in the warehouse.

Choice D is incorrect. The margin of error describes the likely range of the mean, not the battery life of each individual phone.

distractor_notes.A: Treats the sample mean as the exact population mean, ignoring the margin of error.
distractor_notes.B: Generalizes to a larger population (all models) than the one that was randomly sampled.
distractor_notes.D: Applies the range for the mean to every individual phone.

topic: smartphone battery life in video playback
choice_a: The mean battery life of all smartphones of this model in the warehouse is exactly 11.2 hours.
choice_b: The mean battery life of all smartphones of every model in the warehouse is likely between 10.8 and 11.6 hours.
choice_c: The mean battery life of all smartphones of this model in the warehouse is likely between 10.8 and 11.6 hours.
choice_d: The battery life of every smartphone of this model in the warehouse is between 10.8 and 11.6 hours.

skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
stem:
An engineer selected 80 phones at random from all the phones of one model produced at a factory last month. The engineer then randomly assigned 40 of the phones to have power-saving mode turned on and the other 40 to have it turned off. All 80 phones started fully charged and ran the same set of apps for 8 hours. The phones with power-saving mode turned on had a significantly higher remaining charge than the phones with it turned off.

Which of the following conclusions is best supported by the study?
explanation:
Choice A is correct. The phones were randomly assigned to the two groups, so a cause-and-effect conclusion is supported. The phones were also randomly selected from this model produced at the factory last month, so the conclusion applies to that population.

Choice B is incorrect. Only one model from one factory was sampled, so the result can't be extended to all models and manufacturers.

Choice C is incorrect. This was an experiment with random assignment, so it does support a cause-and-effect conclusion.

Choice D is incorrect. Because the phones were selected at random from the factory's output of this model, the result can be applied to that whole population, not just the 40 phones.

distractor_notes.B: Generalizes to a larger, different population than the one randomly sampled.
distractor_notes.C: Misses that random assignment to groups supports a cause-and-effect conclusion.
distractor_notes.D: Overlooks that random sampling allows the result to apply to the whole sampled population.

topic: power-saving mode and remaining charge
choice_a: Using power-saving mode causes phones of this model produced at the factory last month to keep more charge during this kind of use.
choice_b: Using power-saving mode causes phones of all models from every manufacturer to keep more charge during this kind of use.
choice_c: Phones with power-saving mode kept more charge, but the study cannot show that the mode caused the difference in charge.
choice_d: Using power-saving mode caused more charge to be kept, but only for the 40 phones in the study that used the mode.

skill: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
stem:
A delivery company operates 2,400 routes. To check on-time performance, a manager selected 150 of these routes at random and found that 18% of the selected routes had at least one late delivery last week. The associated margin of error for this estimate is 5%.

Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion based on this information?
explanation:
Choice D is correct. The sample was chosen at random from the company's 2,400 routes, so the result applies to those routes. The estimate plus or minus the margin of error, $18\% \pm 5\%$, gives a plausible range of $13\%$ to $23\%$ for the true percent of the company's routes with at least one late delivery.

Choice A is incorrect. The sample percent is only an estimate; the true percent could be any plausible value in the range, not exactly 18%.

Choice B is incorrect. Only this company's routes were sampled, so the result can't be extended to all delivery companies in the state.

Choice C is incorrect. A larger random sample would likely produce a smaller margin of error, not a larger one.

distractor_notes.A: Treats the sample estimate as the exact population value, ignoring the margin of error.
distractor_notes.B: Generalizes the result to a larger population (all delivery companies in the state) that was not sampled.
distractor_notes.C: Believes a larger sample increases the margin of error; it actually tends to decrease it.

topic: delivery company late routes
choice_a: Exactly 18% of the company's 2,400 routes had at least one late delivery last week.
choice_b: It is plausible that between 13% and 23% of all routes run by delivery companies in the state had at least one late delivery last week.
choice_c: If the manager had randomly selected 300 of the company's routes instead, the margin of error would likely be greater than 5%.
choice_d: It is plausible that between 13% and 23% of the company's 2,400 routes had at least one late delivery last week.

stem: A mobile carrier anchors a straight support cable from the top of a vertical cell phone tower to a point on level ground. The cable is $120$ feet long and makes a $30^\circ$ angle with the ground. What is the height, in feet, of the tower?
explanation:
The correct answer is 60. The tower, the ground, and the cable form a right triangle with a $30^\circ$ angle at the ground. The cable is the hypotenuse, so it has length $2x = 120$, which gives $x = 60$. The tower is the side opposite the $30^\circ$ angle, which is the short leg $x$. So the tower is $60$ feet tall.

Check: $120 \sin 30^\circ = 120 \cdot \frac{1}{2} = 60$.

- $60\sqrt{3} \approx 103.9$ is incorrect. This is the long leg: the distance along the ground, which is opposite the $60^\circ$ angle.
- $240$ is incorrect. This treats the cable as the short leg and doubles it.
- $60\sqrt{2} \approx 84.9$ is incorrect. This uses the 45-45-90 pattern, dividing the hypotenuse by $\sqrt{2}$.

distractor_notes.240: Treated the 120-foot cable as the short leg and doubled it to get a hypotenuse.
distractor_notes.103.9 (60√3): Swapped which leg is opposite 30°; this is the horizontal distance along the ground, not the height.
distractor_notes.84.85 (60√2): Used the 45-45-90 pattern, dividing the hypotenuse by √2.
distractor_notes.207.8 (120√3): Multiplied the hypotenuse by √3 as though it were the short leg.

topic: cell tower support cable

stem: A museum is making a sign to point visitors toward a new exhibit. The sign is shaped like a right triangle, and one of its angles measures $30^\circ$. The longest side of the sign is $12$ inches long. What is the length, in inches, of the shortest side of the sign?
explanation:
Choice A is correct. The angles of the sign are $30^\circ$, $60^\circ$, and $90^\circ$, so its sides follow the pattern $x$, $x\sqrt{3}$, $2x$. The longest side is the hypotenuse, so $2x = 12$ and $x = 6$. The shortest side is opposite the $30^\circ$ angle, and its length is $x = 6$ inches.

Choice B is incorrect. This uses the 45-45-90 pattern, dividing the hypotenuse by $\sqrt{2}$.

Choice C is incorrect. This is the side opposite the $60^\circ$ angle, the longer leg, not the shortest side.

Choice D is incorrect. This treats the hypotenuse, $12$, as the short leg and multiplies it by $\sqrt{3}$.

distractor_notes.B: Used the 45-45-90 pattern: $12 \div \sqrt{2} = 6\sqrt{2}$.
distractor_notes.C: Swapped the legs: gave the side opposite $60^\circ$, $6\sqrt{3}$, instead of the side opposite $30^\circ$.
distractor_notes.D: Treated the hypotenuse as the short leg: $12\sqrt{3}$.

topic: triangular museum direction sign

stem: A seating area in a museum's lobby, where visitors rest between galleries, is shaped like a right triangle. One of the triangle's angles measures $45^\circ$, and the side opposite the right angle has a length of $9\sqrt{2}$ feet. What is the length, in feet, of the side opposite the $45^\circ$ angle?
explanation:
The correct answer is 9. Since one acute angle is $45^\circ$, the other is $180^\circ - 90^\circ - 45^\circ = 45^\circ$. So the sides follow the 45-45-90 pattern $x$, $x$, $x\sqrt{2}$. The side opposite the right angle is the hypotenuse, so $x\sqrt{2} = 9\sqrt{2}$, and $x = 9$. The side opposite a $45^\circ$ angle is a leg, so its length is $9$ feet.

Check: legs of $9$ and $9$ give a hypotenuse of $\sqrt{81 + 81} = \sqrt{162} = 9\sqrt{2}$.

distractor_notes.18: Multiplied the hypotenuse by $\sqrt{2}$ instead of dividing: $9\sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{2} = 18$.
distractor_notes.12.72 (about $9\\sqrt{2}$): Gave the hypotenuse itself instead of a leg.
distractor_notes.6.36 (about $\\frac{9\\sqrt{2}}{2}$): Used the 30-60-90 pattern and halved the hypotenuse.

topic: triangular lobby seating area

stem: A cell phone battery is a thin rectangular block. On its largest rectangular face, a designer plans to print a straight charge-indicator stripe from one corner to the opposite corner. The stripe makes a $30^\circ$ angle with the longer side of the face, and the longer side is $9$ centimeters long. What is the length, in centimeters, of the stripe?
explanation:
Choice C is correct. The stripe is a diagonal of the rectangle. It splits the face into two right triangles. In each triangle, the stripe is the hypotenuse, and the longer side of the face is the leg next to the $30^\circ$ angle. That makes it the leg opposite the $60^\circ$ angle, so it is the long leg of a 30-60-90 triangle. The sides follow the pattern $x$, $x\sqrt{3}$, $2x$. Set $x\sqrt{3}=9$, so $x=\frac{9}{\sqrt{3}}=3\sqrt{3}$. The hypotenuse is $2x=6\sqrt{3}$. Check: $\cos 30^\circ=\frac{9}{6\sqrt{3}}=\frac{3}{2\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, which is correct.

Choice A is incorrect. This is $x$, the shorter side of the face, not the stripe.

Choice B is incorrect. This multiplies $9$ by $\cos 30^\circ$ instead of dividing by it. That treats the $9$ cm side as the hypotenuse.

Choice D is incorrect. This treats the $9$ cm side as the short leg, the side opposite $30^\circ$, and doubles it. The $9$ cm side is next to the $30^\circ$ angle, not opposite it.

distractor_notes.A: Found the short leg $x=3\sqrt{3}$ (the shorter side of the face) and stopped instead of doubling it for the hypotenuse.
distractor_notes.B: Computed $9\cos 30^\circ$, which treats the 9 cm side as the hypotenuse instead of dividing by $\cos 30^\circ$.
distractor_notes.D: Swapped which leg is opposite $30^\circ$: treated the 9 cm side as the short leg and doubled it.

topic: cell phone battery charge-indicator stripe

stem:
On a theater's seating chart, two aisles are drawn as parallel lines, and a diagonal walkway is drawn as a line that crosses both aisles. Two of the angles formed are same-side interior angles: they lie between the two aisles and on the same side of the walkway. One of these angles measures $(4x - 20)^\circ$, and the other measures $(2x + 20)^\circ$.

What is the measure, in degrees, of the angle that measures $(2x + 20)^\circ$?
explanation:
Choice C is correct. When a transversal crosses two parallel lines, same-side interior angles are supplementary, so their measures add to $180^\circ$:

$(4x - 20) + (2x + 20) = 180$

$6x = 180$

$x = 30$

Circle what the question asks for: the angle that measures $(2x + 20)^\circ$. That angle is $2(30) + 20 = 80^\circ$. Check: the other angle is $4(30) - 20 = 100^\circ$, and $80 + 100 = 180$.

Choice A is incorrect. This is the value of $x$, not the measure of the angle.

Choice B is incorrect. This comes from setting the two angles equal ($4x - 20 = 2x + 20$, so $x = 20$), but same-side interior angles add to $180^\circ$. They are not equal.

Choice D is incorrect. This is the measure of the other angle, $(4x - 20)^\circ$.

distractor_notes.A: Reported $x = 30$ instead of the angle measure.
distractor_notes.B: Set the angles equal instead of supplementary: $x = 20$, so each angle would be $60^\circ$.
distractor_notes.D: Found the other angle of the pair, $4(30) - 20 = 100$.

topic: theater seating chart aisles and walkway

stem:
In a plane, line $p$ is parallel to line $q$, and both lines are intersected by line $t$. Two same-side interior angles formed by these lines have measures $(3x + 10)^\circ$ and $(2x + 20)^\circ$.

What is the measure, in degrees, of the angle with measure $(3x + 10)^\circ$?
explanation:
Choice D is correct. When parallel lines are cut by a transversal, same-side interior angles are supplementary, so they add to $180^\circ$. That gives $(3x + 10) + (2x + 20) = 180$, so $5x + 30 = 180$, $5x = 150$, and $x = 30$. Circle what the question asks for: it wants the angle, not $x$. The angle is $3(30) + 10 = 100$ degrees. Check: the other angle is $2(30) + 20 = 80$, and $100 + 80 = 180$.

Choice A is incorrect. This is the value of $x$, not the measure of the angle.

Choice B is incorrect. This comes from setting the two angles equal: $3x + 10 = 2x + 20$ gives $x = 10$, and then $3(10) + 10 = 40$. Same-side interior angles add to $180^\circ$. They are not equal.

Choice C is incorrect. This is the measure of the other angle, $(2x + 20)^\circ$, not the angle asked for.

distractor_notes.A: Reported $x = 30$ instead of the angle measure.
distractor_notes.B: Set the angles equal ($3x + 10 = 2x + 20$, so $x = 10$) instead of making them supplementary, then evaluated $3x + 10$.
distractor_notes.C: Found $x$ correctly but gave the other angle of the pair, $2x + 20 = 80$.

topic: same-side interior angles, pure math

stem: An engineer's cross-sectional drawing of a draining water tank shows two parallel horizontal support beams. A straight drain pipe runs diagonally from the upper beam to the lower beam, crossing both. Of the angles that the pipe forms with the beams, two lie between the beams and on the same side of the pipe. One of these angles measures $(2x - 110)^\circ$, and the other measures $(x + 50)^\circ$. What is the measure, in degrees, of the angle that measures $(2x - 110)^\circ$?
explanation:
Choice A is correct. The two angles lie between the parallel beams and on the same side of the pipe, which acts as a transversal. That makes them same-side interior angles, so they add to $180^\circ$: $(2x - 110) + (x + 50) = 180$. This gives $3x - 60 = 180$, so $3x = 240$ and $x = 80$. Circle what the question asks for: the angle, not $x$. The angle is $2(80) - 110 = 50$ degrees. Check: the other angle is $80 + 50 = 130$, and $50 + 130 = 180$.

Choice B is incorrect. This is the value of $x$, not the measure of the angle.

Choice C is incorrect. This is the measure of the other angle, $(x + 50)^\circ$.

Choice D is incorrect. This comes from setting the two angles equal, $2x - 110 = x + 50$, which gives $x = 160$. Same-side interior angles are supplementary, not equal.

distractor_notes.B: Solved correctly for x = 80 but reported x instead of the angle measure.
distractor_notes.C: Found the measure of the other angle of the pair, x + 50 = 130.
distractor_notes.D: Set the angles equal instead of supplementary: 2x − 110 = x + 50 gives x = 160.

topic: drain pipe crossing parallel tank support beams

stem: A farmer measuring crop yield marks off a test plot in the shape of right triangle $PQR$, where angle $Q$ is the right angle. Side $PQ$ is $40$ meters long, side $QR$ is $75$ meters long, and side $PR$ is $85$ meters long. What is the value of $\sin P$?
explanation:
Choice C is correct. The sine of an angle is the opposite side over the hypotenuse. The right angle is at $Q$, so the hypotenuse is $PR = 85$. The side opposite angle $P$ is $QR = 75$. So $\sin P = \frac{75}{85} = \frac{15}{17}$.

Choice A is incorrect. This is $\frac{PQ}{PR}$, the adjacent side over the hypotenuse, which is $\cos P$, not $\sin P$.

Choice B is incorrect. This is $\frac{PQ}{QR}$, the adjacent side over the opposite side, which is $\tan R$, not $\sin P$.

Choice D is incorrect. This is $\frac{QR}{PQ}$, the opposite side over the adjacent side, which is $\tan P$, not $\sin P$.

distractor_notes.A: Used the adjacent leg over the hypotenuse (cos P), or the other leg over the hypotenuse.
distractor_notes.B: Used adjacent over opposite for angle P, which gives tan R.
distractor_notes.D: Used opposite over adjacent (tan P) instead of opposite over hypotenuse.

topic: Triangular test plot for crop yield

stem: For one of its daily orders, a bakery cuts a rectangular sheet cake that measures 24 inches by 10 inches along one diagonal, forming two congruent right triangles. One of these triangles is labeled $PQR$, where angle $Q$ is the right angle, $PQ = 24$ inches, and $QR = 10$ inches. What is the value of $\cos P$?
explanation:
Choice C is correct. First find the hypotenuse: $PR = \sqrt{24^2 + 10^2} = \sqrt{676} = 26$ inches. This is a 5-12-13 triangle scaled by 2. From angle $P$, the adjacent leg is $PQ = 24$, so $\cos P = \frac{24}{26} = \frac{12}{13}$. As a check, angles $P$ and $R$ add up to $90^\circ$. So $\cos P = \sin R$, and $\sin R = \frac{PQ}{PR} = \frac{24}{26} = \frac{12}{13}$.

Choice A is incorrect. This is the opposite leg over the hypotenuse, $\frac{10}{26}$, which is $\sin P$, not $\cos P$.

Choice B is incorrect. This is the opposite leg over the adjacent leg, $\frac{10}{24}$, which is $\tan P$.

Choice D is incorrect. This is the adjacent leg over the opposite leg, $\frac{24}{10}$, which is $\tan R$.

distractor_notes.A: Used the other leg over the hypotenuse (10/26), which gives sin P instead of cos P.
distractor_notes.B: Used opposite over adjacent (10/24), which gives tan P.
distractor_notes.D: Used adjacent over opposite (24/10), which gives tan R (the reciprocal of tan P).

topic: bakery sheet cake cut along a diagonal

stem: On a road trip, a car traveled due east on a straight road from town $P$ to town $Q$. It then traveled due north on a straight road from town $Q$ to town $R$. The car used 4 gallons of fuel between $P$ and $Q$ and 7.5 gallons between $Q$ and $R$. A straight road runs directly from $P$ to $R$, and driving it would have used 8.5 gallons. The car uses fuel at a constant rate per mile. The three towns are the vertices of triangle $PQR$, and the measure of angle $R$ is $b^\circ$. What is the value of $\cos((90-b)^\circ)$?
explanation:
Choice A is correct. The car uses fuel at a constant rate per mile, so each distance is proportional to the fuel used. The sides are in the ratio $4 : 7.5 : 8.5$, which is $8 : 15 : 17$.

The car drove east and then north, so the right angle is at $Q$. Check: $4^2 + 7.5^2 = 16 + 56.25 = 72.25 = 8.5^2$. Side $PR$ is the hypotenuse.

Angles $R$ and $P$ are complementary, so $\cos((90-b)^\circ) = \sin(b^\circ) = \sin R$. The side opposite angle $R$ is $PQ$, so $\sin R = \frac{PQ}{PR} = \frac{4}{8.5} = \frac{8}{17}$.

As a second check, angle $P$ measures $(90-b)^\circ$. Its adjacent side is $PQ$, so $\cos P = \frac{PQ}{PR} = \frac{8}{17}$.

Choice B is incorrect. This is $\frac{PQ}{QR}$, which is opposite over adjacent ($\tan R$), not opposite over hypotenuse.

Choice C is incorrect. This is $\frac{QR}{PR}$, the other leg over the hypotenuse. It equals $\cos R$, not $\cos(90-b)^\circ$.

Choice D is incorrect. This is $\frac{QR}{PQ}$, which is opposite over adjacent from angle $P$ ($\tan P$).

distractor_notes.B: Used opposite/adjacent from angle R (tan R = 4/7.5 = 8/15) instead of opposite/hypotenuse.
distractor_notes.C: Used the other leg over the hypotenuse (adjacent/hypotenuse for angle R), giving cos R = 15/17 instead of sin R.
distractor_notes.D: Used opposite/adjacent from angle P (tan P = 7.5/4 = 15/8).

topic: road trip fuel use between three towns

stem:
A wireless charging pad charges a cell phone's battery whenever the phone is placed within a circular region on the pad. In the $xy$-plane, where each unit is 1 centimeter, the boundary of this region is the circle with equation $x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 4y - 12 = 0$.

What is the radius, in centimeters, of this circle?
explanation:
Choice C is correct. Move the constant to the right side: $x^2 - 6x + y^2 + 4y = 12$. Complete the square for each variable. Half of $-6$ is $-3$, and $(-3)^2 = 9$. Half of $4$ is $2$, and $2^2 = 4$. Add both squares to both sides: $(x^2 - 6x + 9) + (y^2 + 4y + 4) = 12 + 9 + 4$, so $(x - 3)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 25$. Since $r^2 = 25$, find r first: $r = \sqrt{25} = 5$.

Choice A is incorrect. This comes from adding 9 and 4 only to the left side, which gives $r^2 = 12$ and $r = \sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}$.

Choice B is incorrect. This comes from adding only the 9 to the right side and forgetting the 4, which gives $r^2 = 21$.

Choice D is incorrect. This is $r^2$, not the radius.

distractor_notes.A: Forgot to add the squares (9 and 4) to the right side, so took $r^2 = 12$ and $r = 2\sqrt{3}$.
distractor_notes.B: Added only the $x$-square (9) to the right side, so took $r^2 = 21$.
distractor_notes.D: Gave $r^2 = 25$ as the radius instead of taking its square root.

topic: wireless phone charging pad region

stem: The equation $x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 10y - 2 = 0$ defines a circle in the $xy$-plane. Which of the following gives the center and the radius of the circle?
explanation:
Choice C is correct. Move the constant: $x^2 - 6x + y^2 + 10y = 2$. Add $(\frac{-6}{2})^2 = 9$ and $(\frac{10}{2})^2 = 25$ to both sides: $x^2 - 6x + 9 + y^2 + 10y + 25 = 2 + 9 + 25$. This gives $(x - 3)^2 + (y + 5)^2 = 36$. The center is $(3, -5)$ and the radius is $\sqrt{36} = 6$. Check: expanding $(x-3)^2 + (y+5)^2 = 36$ gives $x^2 - 6x + 9 + y^2 + 10y + 25 - 36 = 0$, or $x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 10y - 2 = 0$.

Choice A is incorrect. This flips the signs of the center. In $(x - 3)^2$, the $x$-coordinate is $+3$; in $(y + 5)^2$, the $y$-coordinate is $-5$.

Choice B is incorrect. This adds $9$ and $25$ to the left side only, leaving $2$ on the right, so $r^2 = 2$.

Choice D is incorrect. This is $r^2$, not $r$. The radius is the square root of $36$.

distractor_notes.A: Center signs flipped: read $(x-3)^2 + (y+5)^2$ as center $(-3, 5)$.
distractor_notes.B: Forgot to add the squares ($9$ and $25$) to the right side, so $r^2 = 2$ and $r = \sqrt{2}$.
distractor_notes.D: Gave $r^2 = 36$ as the radius instead of taking the square root.

topic: center and radius from general form

stem:
$$x^2 + y^2 + 8x - 2y = 32$$

The equation above defines a circle in the $xy$-plane. What is the radius of the circle?
explanation:
Choice C is correct. Complete the square for each variable. Half of $8$ is $4$, and $4^2 = 16$. Half of $-2$ is $-1$, and $(-1)^2 = 1$. Add both squares to both sides: $x^2 + 8x + 16 + y^2 - 2y + 1 = 32 + 16 + 1$. This gives $(x + 4)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 49$. So $r^2 = 49$, and the radius is $r = \sqrt{49} = 7$.

Choice A is incorrect. This comes from completing the squares on the left but not adding $16$ and $1$ to the right side, giving $r = \sqrt{32} = 4\sqrt{2}$.

Choice B is incorrect. This comes from adding only the $16$ for the $x$-terms to the right side and forgetting the $1$ for the $y$-terms, giving $r = \sqrt{48} = 4\sqrt{3}$.

Choice D is incorrect. This is $r^2$, not $r$. Take the square root to find the radius.

distractor_notes.A: Forgot to add the squares (16 and 1) to the right side; took $\sqrt{32}$.
distractor_notes.B: Added 16 for the x-terms but forgot to add 1 for the y-terms; took $\sqrt{48}$.
distractor_notes.D: Gave $r^2 = 49$ as the radius instead of taking the square root.

topic: abstract circle equation, radius

stem: A print shop is filling an order for posters that each display a circular seal. In the shop's layout software, each poster is modeled in the $xy$-plane with its left edge along the $y$-axis. The boundary of the seal is given by the equation $3x^2 + 3y^2 - 18x - 30y + c = 0$, where $c$ is a constant. For this order, the seal must touch the poster's left edge at exactly one point. What is the value of $c$?
explanation:
Choice C is correct. First divide every term by $3$: $x^2 + y^2 - 6x - 10y + \frac{c}{3} = 0$. Move the constant: $x^2 - 6x + y^2 - 10y = -\frac{c}{3}$. Add $(-3)^2 = 9$ and $(-5)^2 = 25$ to both sides: $(x-3)^2 + (y-5)^2 = 34 - \frac{c}{3}$. The center is $(3, 5)$ no matter what $c$ is. The seal touches the $y$-axis at exactly one point, so the radius equals the distance from the center to the $y$-axis, which is $3$. So $r^2 = 9$, and $34 - \frac{c}{3} = 9$. This gives $\frac{c}{3} = 25$, so $c = 75$. Check: with $x = 0$, the equation becomes $3y^2 - 30y + 75 = 0$, or $3(y-5)^2 = 0$. That has exactly one solution, $y = 5$.

Choice A is incorrect. This is $\frac{c}{3}$, not $c$. It comes from not multiplying back by $3$, or from forgetting to divide the constant by $3$. Circle what the question asks for.

Choice B is incorrect. This uses the distance from the center to the $x$-axis, $5$, as the radius: $34 - \frac{c}{3} = 25$ gives $c = 27$. That circle would touch the $x$-axis, not the $y$-axis.

Choice D is incorrect. This sets the right side equal to $r = 3$ instead of $r^2 = 9$: $34 - \frac{c}{3} = 3$ gives $c = 93$.

distractor_notes.A: Solved for c/3 = 25 and stopped, or divided the x and y terms by 3 but left c unchanged.
distractor_notes.B: Used the y-coordinate of the center, 5, as the radius. This is the tangent-to-the-x-axis condition, not the y-axis condition.
distractor_notes.D: Treated the right side 34 − c/3 as r instead of r², setting it equal to 3 rather than 9.

topic: print shop poster seal touching the left edge

stem: A quality-control inspector examines a sample metal disk in the shape of a circle with radius $12$ millimeters. She marks an arc along the edge of the disk that has a central angle of $60^\circ$. The length of this arc is $k\pi$ millimeters. What is the value of $k$?
explanation:
The correct answer is 4. An arc is a fraction of the circle's circumference. The fraction is $\frac{60}{360} = \frac{1}{6}$. The circumference is $2\pi r = 2\pi(12) = 24\pi$ millimeters. So the arc length is $\frac{1}{6}(24\pi) = 4\pi$ millimeters, and $k = 4$.

Check: six of these $4\pi$ arcs make the full circle, $6(4\pi) = 24\pi$, which matches the circumference.

- $24$ is incorrect. This uses the area, $\pi r^2 = 144\pi$, instead of the circumference: $\frac{1}{6}(144\pi) = 24\pi$.
- $8$ is incorrect. This uses the diameter, $24$, as the radius: $\frac{1}{6}(2\pi \cdot 24) = 8\pi$.
- $2$ is incorrect. This uses $\pi r$ instead of $2\pi r$ for the circumference: $\frac{1}{6}(12\pi) = 2\pi$.

distractor_notes.2: Used $\pi r = 12\pi$ as the circumference, forgetting the factor of 2.
distractor_notes.8: Used the diameter, 24, as the radius, giving a circumference of $48\pi$.
distractor_notes.24: Used the area $\pi r^2 = 144\pi$ instead of the circumference, then took $\frac{1}{6}$ of it.

stem: A bacteria culture is grown in a circular petri dish with a diameter of 90 millimeters. A researcher marks two points on the rim of the dish. The segments from the center of the dish to these two points form a central angle of $\frac{4\pi}{9}$ radians. What is the length, in millimeters, of the shorter arc of the rim between the two marked points?
explanation:
Choice B is correct. The diameter is 90 millimeters, so the radius is $r = 45$ millimeters. When the central angle is in radians, arc length is $s = r\theta$. So $s = 45 \cdot \frac{4\pi}{9} = 20\pi$ millimeters. Check in degrees: $\frac{4\pi}{9} \cdot \frac{180}{\pi} = 80^\circ$, and $\frac{80}{360} \cdot 2\pi(45) = \frac{2}{9} \cdot 90\pi = 20\pi$. Because $\frac{4\pi}{9} < \pi$, this is the shorter arc.

Choice A is incorrect. This is $\frac{1}{2}r\theta$, which mixes up the arc length formula with the sector area formula $\frac{1}{2}r^2\theta$.

Choice C is incorrect. This uses the diameter, 90, as the radius: $90 \cdot \frac{4\pi}{9} = 40\pi$.

Choice D is incorrect. This is the area of the sector, $\frac{1}{2}(45)^2 \cdot \frac{4\pi}{9} = 450\pi$, not the length of the arc.

distractor_notes.A: Computed $\frac{1}{2}r\theta$, blending the arc length formula with the sector area formula.
distractor_notes.C: Used the diameter (90) as the radius in $s = r\theta$.
distractor_notes.D: Found the sector area $\frac{1}{2}r^2\theta$ (area, using $\pi r^2$) instead of the arc length.

stem: At a children's museum, two visitors ride an indoor carousel that rotates about its center. One visitor rides at the carousel's outer edge, and the other rides $1.5$ meters closer to the center. While the carousel rotates through an angle of $x^\circ$, where $0 < x < 360$, the visitor at the outer edge travels $3$ meters farther along a circular path than the other visitor does. What is the value of $x$?
explanation:
Choice D is correct. Let $R$ be the radius of the outer edge. The other visitor rides on a circle of radius $R - 1.5$. During a rotation of $x^\circ$, each visitor travels an arc of $\frac{x}{360}\cdot 2\pi \cdot (\text{radius})$. The difference is $\frac{x}{360}\cdot 2\pi R - \frac{x}{360}\cdot 2\pi(R - 1.5) = \frac{x}{360}\cdot 2\pi(1.5) = \frac{x}{360}\cdot 3\pi$. The radius $R$ cancels, so you never need it. Set the difference equal to $3$: $\frac{x}{360}\cdot 3\pi = 3$, so $\frac{x}{360} = \frac{1}{\pi}$ and $x = \frac{360}{\pi}$, about $114.6$. Check in radians: arc length is $r\theta$, so the difference is $1.5\theta = 3$. That gives $\theta = 2$ radians, and $2 \cdot \frac{180}{\pi} = \frac{360}{\pi}$ degrees.

Choice A is incorrect. This comes from converting $2$ radians to degrees with the conversion inverted: $2 \cdot \frac{\pi}{180} = \frac{\pi}{90}$.

Choice B is incorrect. This is the angle in radians. The question asks for degrees, and $2$ radians must still be converted.

Choice C is incorrect. This comes from using diameters in place of radii. The $1.5$-meter difference becomes $3$ meters, so the angle comes out half as large.

distractor_notes.A: Found 2 radians but converted with the factor inverted: 2 × π/180 = π/90.
distractor_notes.B: Stopped at the radian measure (θ = 2) and did not convert it to degrees, even though the angle is given as x°.
distractor_notes.C: Used diameters instead of radii, so the difference became 3 meters: (x/360)·2π·3 = 3, giving x = 180/π.

stem: A circular park has a fountain at its center, $O$. Two straight paths run from $O$ to points $A$ and $B$ on the park's circular boundary. The region enclosed by these two paths and the shorter arc $AB$ is a wildflower meadow. The shorter arc $AB$ has a length of $10\pi$ meters, and the area of the part of the park outside the meadow is $750\pi$ square meters. The measure of angle $AOB$ is $k\pi$ radians. What is the value of $k$?
explanation:
The correct answer is 1/3.

Let $r$ be the radius in meters and $\theta$ the measure of angle $AOB$ in radians.

- Arc length: $r\theta = 10\pi$.
- Meadow (sector) area: $\frac{1}{2}r^2\theta = \frac{1}{2}r(r\theta) = \frac{1}{2}r(10\pi) = 5\pi r$.
- The part outside the meadow is the whole park minus the meadow: $\pi r^2 - 5\pi r = 750\pi$.

Divide by $\pi$: $r^2 - 5r - 750 = 0$, so $(r - 30)(r + 25) = 0$. A radius can't be negative, so $r = 30$.

Then $\theta = \frac{10\pi}{30} = \frac{\pi}{3}$ radians, which is $60^\circ$. Circle what the question asks for: $\theta = k\pi$, so $k = \frac{1}{3}$.

Check: the circumference is $60\pi$, and $10\pi$ is $\frac{1}{6}$ of it, so the angle is $\frac{360^\circ}{6} = 60^\circ$. The park's area is $900\pi$, the meadow's is $\frac{1}{6}(900\pi) = 150\pi$, and $900\pi - 150\pi = 750\pi$. ✓

- 1/15 is incorrect. This treats $750\pi$ as the meadow's area instead of the area outside it.
- 5/3 is incorrect. This is the angle for the longer arc, the part outside the meadow.
- 1/6 is incorrect. This is the fraction of the circle, not the coefficient of $\pi$. The angle is $\frac{1}{6}(2\pi) = \frac{\pi}{3}$.
- 60 is incorrect. This is the angle in degrees, not radians.
- 1.047 is incorrect. This is the full radian measure $\frac{\pi}{3}$, not $k$.

distractor_notes.60: Gave the degree measure and never converted to radians.
distractor_notes.1/15: Used $750\pi$ as the meadow's area. That gives $r = 150$ and a $12^\circ$ angle, which is $\frac{\pi}{15}$ radians.
distractor_notes.5/3: Found the angle for the longer arc, $2\pi - \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{5\pi}{3}$, instead of angle $AOB$.
distractor_notes.1/6: Reported the meadow's fraction of the circle, forgetting that a full circle is $2\pi$ radians, not $\pi$.
distractor_notes.1.047: Entered the decimal value of $\frac{\pi}{3}$ instead of the coefficient $k$.

stem: A bike-share program displays its station map on two similar rectangular panels. The larger panel has a width of 6 feet and an area of 18 square feet. The smaller panel has a width of 4 feet. What is the area, in square feet, of the smaller panel?
explanation:
Choice B is correct. The panels are similar, so the scale factor from the larger panel to the smaller panel is $k = \frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}$. Areas scale by $k^2 = \frac{4}{9}$. The smaller panel's area is $18 \cdot \frac{4}{9} = 8$ square feet. Check: the larger panel is $6$ by $3$ feet, so the smaller panel is $4$ by $2$ feet, and $4 \cdot 2 = 8$.

Choice A is incorrect. This scales the area by $k^3 = \frac{8}{27}$, which is the rule for volume, not area.

Choice C is incorrect. This scales the area by $k = \frac{2}{3}$, which is the rule for lengths, not area.

Choice D is incorrect. This scales in the wrong direction, multiplying by $\left(\frac{6}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{4}$ instead of $\left(\frac{4}{6}\right)^2$.

distractor_notes.A: Scaled the area by k³ = 8/27, as for a volume.
distractor_notes.C: Scaled the area by k = 2/3, as for a length.
distractor_notes.D: Scaled the wrong direction, multiplying by (6/4)² = 9/4.

stem: An online store sets its shipping fees based on the volume of the box an order is packed in. The store's medium box and large box are similar rectangular prisms. The longest edge of the large box is $45$ centimeters, and the longest edge of the medium box is $30$ centimeters. The volume of the large box is $27{,}000$ cubic centimeters. What is the volume, in cubic centimeters, of the medium box?
explanation:
Choice A is correct. The boxes are similar, so the length scale factor from the large box to the medium box is $k = \frac{30}{45} = \frac{2}{3}$. Volumes scale by $k^3$, so the medium box's volume is $27{,}000 \cdot \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^3 = 27{,}000 \cdot \frac{8}{27} = 8{,}000$ cubic centimeters. Check: $\frac{8{,}000}{27{,}000} = \frac{8}{27} = \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^3$.

Choice B is incorrect. This scales the volume by $k^2 = \frac{4}{9}$, which is the area ratio, not the volume ratio.

Choice C is incorrect. This scales the volume by $k = \frac{2}{3}$, the length ratio, instead of cubing it.

Choice D is incorrect. This cubes the scale factor in the wrong direction, multiplying by $\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{27}{8}$, which gives a volume larger than the large box's.

distractor_notes.B: Scaled the volume by k² = 4/9 (area ratio) instead of k³.
distractor_notes.C: Scaled the volume by k = 2/3 (length ratio) instead of k³.
distractor_notes.D: Scaled the wrong direction: multiplied by (3/2)³ = 27/8 instead of (2/3)³.

stem: In a wildlife population study, biologists model gray seals of different sizes as geometrically similar solids with the same density. In this model, each seal's mass is proportional to its volume. Seal A has a mass of 64 kilograms, and seal B has a mass of 216 kilograms. For seal A, the ratio of surface area to volume is $r$. Based on the model, which expression represents the ratio of surface area to volume for seal B?
explanation:
Choice B is correct. The seals have the same density, so the volume ratio equals the mass ratio: $\frac{216}{64} = \frac{27}{8}$. Volumes scale by $k^3$, so $k^3 = \frac{27}{8}$ and the length scale factor is $k = \frac{3}{2}$. Surface areas scale by $k^2 = \frac{9}{4}$. Circle what the question asks for: the ratio of surface area to volume. For seal B, that ratio is $\frac{\frac{9}{4}S_A}{\frac{27}{8}V_A} = \frac{9}{4} \cdot \frac{8}{27} \cdot \frac{S_A}{V_A} = \frac{2}{3}r$. Check with cubes of side 4 and 6 (volumes 64 and 216): the ratios are $\frac{96}{64} = \frac{3}{2}$ and $\frac{216}{216} = 1$, and $1 = \frac{2}{3} \cdot \frac{3}{2}$.

Choice A is incorrect. This divides $r$ by the area factor $\frac{9}{4}$. It ignores that the volume also grows.

Choice C is incorrect. This scales by $k = \frac{3}{2}$ in the wrong direction. It can also come from dividing the volume factor by the area factor instead of the area factor by the volume factor. The larger seal has the smaller ratio.

Choice D is incorrect. This multiplies $r$ by the area factor $\frac{9}{4}$. It forgets that the volume grows by an even larger factor.

distractor_notes.A: Divided r by the area scale factor 9/4 and ignored the growth in volume.
distractor_notes.C: Scaled by k = 3/2 in the wrong direction, or computed (27/8) ÷ (9/4) instead of (9/4) ÷ (27/8).
distractor_notes.D: Multiplied r by the area scale factor 9/4 and forgot that volume grows by 27/8.

stem: A safety guideline for leaning a ladder against a vertical wall states that for every 4 feet of height the top of the ladder reaches on the wall, the base of the ladder should be 1 foot away from the wall. A ladder is placed according to this guideline with its base 3 feet from the wall. How many feet up the wall does the top of the ladder reach?
explanation:
Choice D is correct. Keep the same units in the same position: $\frac{\text{height}}{\text{base}} = \frac{4}{1} = \frac{h}{3}$. Cross-multiplying gives $h = 4 \times 3 = 12$ feet. Check: the height is 4 times the base distance, and $12 = 4 \times 3$.

Choice A is incorrect. This flips one side of the proportion ($\frac{4}{1} = \frac{3}{h}$), which divides 3 by 4 instead of multiplying.

Choice B is incorrect. This divides 4 by 3 instead of multiplying 4 by 3.

Choice C is incorrect. This adds 4 and 3. A proportional relationship scales by multiplying, not adding.

distractor_notes.A: Flipped one side of the proportion, giving $3 \div 4$.
distractor_notes.B: Divided 4 by 3 instead of multiplying.
distractor_notes.C: Added the numbers ($4 + 3$) instead of scaling the ratio.

stem: A rate of $5$ cubic feet per minute is equivalent to how many cubic inches per second? (1 foot = 12 inches)
explanation:
Choice D is correct. A cube that is 1 foot on each side is 12 inches on each side, so $1\text{ ft}^3 = 12^3 = 1{,}728\text{ in}^3$. There are 60 seconds in a minute. Multiply by fractions equal to 1 so the units cancel:

$\frac{5\text{ ft}^3}{1\text{ min}} \cdot \frac{1{,}728\text{ in}^3}{1\text{ ft}^3} \cdot \frac{1\text{ min}}{60\text{ s}} = \frac{8{,}640}{60} = 144$ cubic inches per second.

Check: $144 \times 60 = 8{,}640$ cubic inches per minute, and $8{,}640 \div 1{,}728 = 5$ cubic feet per minute.

Choice A is incorrect. This uses the plain length factor, $1\text{ ft}^3 = 12\text{ in}^3$: $\frac{5 \cdot 12}{60} = 1$.

Choice B is incorrect. This divides by 3,600 (seconds in an hour) instead of 60 (seconds in a minute): $\frac{8{,}640}{3{,}600} = 2.4$.

Choice C is incorrect. This uses the square-unit factor, $1\text{ ft}^3 = 144\text{ in}^3$: $\frac{5 \cdot 144}{60} = 12$.

distractor_notes.A: Converted cubic feet with the plain length factor 12 instead of 12^3 = 1,728.
distractor_notes.B: Mixed time units: divided by 3,600 (seconds per hour) instead of 60 (seconds per minute).
distractor_notes.C: Converted cubic feet with the square factor 144 instead of 1,728.

stem: A shipping company uses a rectangular box with a volume of 240 cubic inches. The company designs a new rectangular box whose volume is 15% greater than the volume of the original box. What is the volume, in cubic inches, of the new box?
explanation:
The correct answer is 276. An increase of 15% means multiplying by $1 + 0.15 = 1.15$. The new volume is $240(1.15) = 276$ cubic inches.

Check: 15% of 240 is $0.15(240) = 36$, and $240 + 36 = 276$.

- 36 is incorrect. This is only the increase, not the new volume.
- 204 is incorrect. This treats the change as a 15% decrease: $240(0.85) = 204$.
- 255 is incorrect. This adds 15 cubic inches instead of 15%.

distractor_notes.36: Found 15% of 240 (the amount of increase) but did not add it to the original volume.
distractor_notes.204: Multiplied by 0.85, treating the 15% increase as a decrease.
distractor_notes.255: Added 15 directly to 240 instead of adding 15% of 240.

stem: A theater's seating chart shows a total of $480$ seats. Of these seats, $35\%$ are in the balcony, and the rest are on the main floor. How many seats are on the main floor?
explanation: The correct answer is 312. If $35\%$ of the seats are in the balcony, then $100\% - 35\% = 65\%$ of the seats are on the main floor. Part = percent × whole, so the main floor has $0.65 \times 480 = 312$ seats. Check: the balcony has $0.35 \times 480 = 168$ seats, and $168 + 312 = 480$. Circle what the question asks for: the main floor, not the balcony.

distractor_notes.65: Gave the percent of seats on the main floor instead of the number of seats.
distractor_notes.168: Found the number of balcony seats ($0.35 \times 480$) instead of main-floor seats.
distractor_notes.445: Subtracted the percent as if it were a number of seats ($480 - 35$).

stem: In a poll of 800 town residents, $30\%$ said they supported a plan to build a new library branch. Six months later, the same 800 residents were polled again, and 180 of them said they supported the plan. By what percent did the number of residents who supported the plan decrease from the first poll to the second poll?
explanation:
Choice B is correct. In the first poll, $0.30 \times 800 = 240$ residents supported the plan. In the second poll, 180 did. The decrease is $240 - 180 = 60$ residents. Percent change compares the change to the old value: $\frac{60}{240} = 0.25$, a $25\%$ decrease. Check: $240 \times (1 - 0.25) = 240 \times 0.75 = 180$.

Choice A is incorrect. This is the drop in percentage points ($30\% - 22.5\%$), not the percent decrease in the number of supporters.

Choice C is incorrect. This divides the change by the new value: $\frac{60}{180}$. Percent change divides by the old value.

Choice D is incorrect. This is the second count as a percent of the first ($\frac{180}{240}$), which is what remains, not the decrease.

distractor_notes.A: Subtracted the support rates ($30\% - 22.5\%$) and gave the percentage-point difference instead of the percent change.
distractor_notes.C: Divided the change of 60 by the new value, 180, instead of the old value, 240.
distractor_notes.D: Computed $\frac{180}{240}$, the fraction that remains, instead of the fraction that was lost.

stem: A water tank is being drained for cleaning. From 8:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m., the amount of water in the tank decreased by 48.8%. For each of these three hours, the amount of water in the tank at the end of the hour was $p\%$ less than the amount at the start of that hour, where $p$ is a constant. The amount of water in the tank at 9:00 a.m. was what percent greater than the amount at 11:00 a.m.?
explanation:
Choice D is correct. Each hour the amount is multiplied by the same factor $m = 1 - \frac{p}{100}$. Successive changes multiply, so over three hours $m^3 = 1 - 0.488 = 0.512$. Then $m = \sqrt[3]{0.512} = 0.8$, so the tank loses 20% each hour.

Let $A$ be the amount at 8:00 a.m. At 9:00 a.m. the tank holds $0.8A$. At 11:00 a.m. it holds $0.512A$. Circle what the question asks for: the 9:00 a.m. amount compared with the 11:00 a.m. amount, so the 11:00 a.m. amount is the base.

$\frac{0.8A - 0.512A}{0.512A} = \frac{0.288}{0.512} = 0.5625$, or 56.25%.

Check: start with 1,000 gallons. The amounts are 800, 640 and 512 gallons. The total drop is $\frac{488}{1{,}000} = 48.8\%$, and $\frac{800 - 512}{512} = 0.5625$.

Choice A is incorrect. This is the difference, $0.288A$, as a percent of the 8:00 a.m. amount instead of the 11:00 a.m. amount.

Choice B is incorrect. This divides by the 9:00 a.m. amount. It is the percent decrease from 9:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m., not how much greater the 9:00 a.m. amount is.

Choice C is incorrect. This adds the two hourly 20% decreases instead of multiplying the factors.

distractor_notes.A: Took the difference between the 9:00 and 11:00 amounts, 0.288A, as a percent of the original 8:00 a.m. amount instead of the 11:00 a.m. amount.
distractor_notes.B: Used the 9:00 a.m. amount as the base: (0.8 − 0.512)/0.8 = 0.36. This is the percent decrease from 9 to 11, not the percent greater.
distractor_notes.C: Found the 20% hourly decrease but added the two hours' decreases (20% + 20%) instead of multiplying the factors.

stem: A runner's pace during a marathon is modeled by the function $P(k) = 0.0025k^2 + 0.02k + 5$, where $P(k)$ is the pace, in minutes per kilometer, $k$ kilometers after the start of the race. According to the model, how many kilometers after the start is the runner's pace 5.6 minutes per kilometer?
explanation:
Choice A is correct. Test the choices by plugging each one into $P(k)$. For $k = 12$: $P(12) = 0.0025(144) + 0.02(12) + 5 = 0.36 + 0.24 + 5 = 5.6$. This is the pace the question asks for. You can also solve it directly: $0.0025k^2 + 0.02k + 5 = 5.6$ becomes $k^2 + 8k - 240 = 0$, which factors as $(k + 20)(k - 12) = 0$. Distance can't be negative, so $k = 12$.

Choice B is incorrect. This is the root $k = -20$ with its sign dropped; $P(20) = 6.4$, not 5.6.

Choice C is incorrect. This comes from treating $k^2$ as $2k$, which gives $0.005k + 0.02k = 0.6$; $P(24) = 6.92$, not 5.6.

Choice D is incorrect. This comes from ignoring the squared term and solving $0.02k = 0.6$; $P(30) = 7.85$, not 5.6.

**Desmos check:** Enter $P(k)=0.0025k^2+0.02k+5$, then type P([12,20,24,30]); only the first entry gives 5.6 (the list returns 5.6, 6.4, 6.92, 7.85).

distractor_notes.B: Factors $k^2 + 8k - 240$ as $(k+20)(k-12)$ but takes 20 from the wrong factor, dropping the negative sign; $P(20) = 6.4$.
distractor_notes.D: Ignores the $0.0025k^2$ term and solves $0.02k = 0.6$ to get 30; $P(30) = 7.85$.

stem:
$$\sqrt{2x+7} = x-4$$

Which of the following is a solution to the given equation?
explanation:
Choice C is correct. Test each choice in the original equation.

- $x=1$: $\sqrt{9}=3$, but $1-4=-3$. Not a solution.
- $x=5$: $\sqrt{17}\approx 4.12$, but $5-4=1$. Not a solution.
- $x=9$: $\sqrt{25}=5$, and $9-4=5$. This works.
- $x=10$: $\sqrt{27}\approx 5.20$, but $10-4=6$. Not a solution.

Solving by hand gives the same result. Squaring both sides gives $2x+7=x^2-8x+16$, so $x^2-10x+9=0$ and $(x-1)(x-9)=0$. Squaring can add a false root, so check both. Only $x=9$ works in the original equation.

Choice A is incorrect. This value is the extraneous root from squaring. It makes the left side $3$ and the right side $-3$, and a square root can't equal a negative number.

Choice B is incorrect. This is the value of each side when $x=9$, not the value of $x$.

Choice D is incorrect. This is the sum of the roots of $x^2-10x+9=0$, not a solution.

**Desmos check:** Enter f(x)=sqrt(2x+7)-(x-4), then f([1,5,9,10]); only the third entry is 0, so x = 9.

distractor_notes.A: Extraneous root from squaring. The student solves $x^2-10x+9=0$ and doesn't check $x=1$ in the original equation, where $3\neq -3$.
distractor_notes.B: Gives the common value of both sides at the solution ($\sqrt{25}=9-4=5$) instead of $x$.
distractor_notes.D: Takes the sum of the roots ($10$, from the $-10x$ coefficient) instead of solving for a root.

stem:
The functions $f$ and $g$ give the total fee, in dollars, to rent a car for $x$ days from Company P and Company Q, respectively.

$f(x) = 35x + 60$

$g(x) = 40x + 20$

A traveler on a 10-day trip rented a car from Company P for the first part of the trip and from Company Q for the rest of the trip. The traveler rented from each company for a positive number of days. The average fee per day for the Company P rental was equal to the average fee per day for the Company Q rental. (The average fee per day for a rental is the total fee for that rental divided by the number of days.) What was the traveler's total fee, in dollars, for the two rentals?
explanation:
Choice B is correct. Let $x$ be the number of days rented from Company P. Then the Company Q rental lasted $10 - x$ days, with $0 < x < 10$. The average fees per day are $\frac{35x+60}{x} = 35 + \frac{60}{x}$ and $\frac{40(10-x)+20}{10-x} = 40 + \frac{20}{10-x}$. Setting them equal gives $\frac{60}{x} - \frac{20}{10-x} = 5$. Multiply both sides by $x(10-x)$: $600 - 80x = 50x - 5x^2$, so $x^2 - 26x + 120 = 0$ and $(x-6)(x-20) = 0$. The root $x = 20$ is impossible, because it would leave $-10$ days for Company Q. So $x = 6$, and the total fee is $f(6) + g(4) = 270 + 180 = 450$.

Faster route: both averages equal the same value $a$, so the total for all 10 days is $10a$. Test each choice $T$ with $a = \frac{T}{10}$. For $T = 450$, $a = 45$. Then $35 + \frac{60}{x} = 45$ gives $x = 6$, and Company Q's average for the other 4 days is $\frac{g(4)}{4} = \frac{180}{4} = 45$. It works. Circle what the question asks for: the total fee, not $x$.

Choice A is incorrect. This comes from the root $x = 20$. Both averages are \$38 there, but that would mean renting from Company Q for $-10$ days.

Choice C is incorrect. This charges Company P for 4 days and Company Q for 6 days: $f(4) + g(6) = 200 + 260 = 460$. The 6 days belong to Company P.

Choice D is incorrect. This adds the one-time fees of \$60 and \$20 to $10 \times 45 = 450$. The averages already include those fees.

**Desmos check:** Define g(x)=40x+20, then enter T=[380,450,460,530], d=60/(T/10-35), and g(10-d)/(10-d)-T/10. The result is 0 only for 380 (where d=20, which is impossible) and 450 (where d=6), so the answer is 450.

distractor_notes.A: Uses the extraneous root x = 20 of the cleared equation (both averages equal \$38, so 10 × 38 = 380), which would require a negative number of days with Company Q.
distractor_notes.C: Solves correctly for x = 6 but then assigns 4 days to Company P and 6 days to Company Q: f(4) + g(6) = 200 + 260 = 460.
distractor_notes.D: Finds the common average of \$45 and multiplies by 10 days, then adds the one-time fees (\$60 + \$20) again, double-counting them: 450 + 80 = 530.

topic: two car rental companies on a split 10-day trip

stem:
An architecture student is assembling a scale model of an office building on a display base. The linear function $h$ gives the total height $h(n)$, in centimeters, of the model, including the base, when the model has $n$ floors. The table shows four values of $h(n)$.

| $n$ | $h(n)$ |
|:---:|:---:|
| 3 | 8.5 |
| 7 | 14.5 |
| 11 | 20.5 |
| 15 | 26.5 |

What is the value of $h(24)$?
explanation:
The correct answer is 40.

Find the slope first. From $n = 3$ to $n = 7$, the height goes from 8.5 to 14.5. That is a change of 6 centimeters over 4 floors, so the slope is $\frac{6}{4} = 1.5$ centimeters per floor.

Next, find the intercept. Using the point $(3, 8.5)$: $8.5 = 1.5(3) + b$, so $b = 8.5 - 4.5 = 4$. The base is 4 centimeters tall, and $h(n) = 1.5n + 4$.

Check with another row: $h(15) = 1.5(15) + 4 = 26.5$. ✓

Circle what the question asks for: $h(24) = 1.5(24) + 4 = 36 + 4 = 40$.

Likely wrong answers:
- 134.5: This uses 6 as the slope. But 6 is the change in height over 4 floors, not over 1 floor.
- 44.5: This uses the first row's height, 8.5, as the intercept. The first row is at $n = 3$, not $n = 0$.
- 36: This multiplies $1.5 \times 24$ but leaves out the 4-centimeter base.

**Desmos check:** Enter the table as $x_1, y_1$, run $y_1 \sim mx_1 + b$ to get $m = 1.5$ and $b = 4$, then type $1.5(24) + 4$ to see 40.

distractor_notes.36: Found the correct slope but dropped the intercept (the 4-centimeter base), computing only $1.5 \times 24$.
distractor_notes.134.5: Took the slope as the change in $h$ between rows (6) and ignored that $n$ steps by 4, giving $h(n) = 6n - 9.5$.
distractor_notes.44.5: Used the first table value, 8.5, as the y-intercept even though it occurs at $n = 3$, not $n = 0$.

stem:
A straight highway runs east from a city's center, and a map of the region shows part of the highway. For a point on the highway, the linear function $f$ gives the actual distance, in kilometers, of the point from the city center. Here $x$ is the distance, in centimeters, of the point on the map from the map's western edge. The table shows several values of $x$ and their corresponding values of $f(x)$.

| $x$ | $f(x)$ |
|:---:|:---:|
| $4$ | $22$ |
| $10$ | $37$ |
| $16$ | $52$ |
| $22$ | $67$ |

What is the value of $f(0)$?
explanation:
Choice B is correct. Each time $x$ increases by $6$, $f(x)$ increases by $15$. So the slope is $\frac{15}{6}=2.5$: each centimeter on the map represents $2.5$ kilometers. Work back from the first row. Going from $x=4$ to $x=0$ lowers $x$ by $4$, so $f(x)$ drops by $4(2.5)=10$. That gives $f(0)=22-10=12$. Check: $f(x)=2.5x+12$ gives $f(22)=55+12=67$.

Choice A is incorrect. This is the slope (the map's scale), not $f(0)$.

Choice C is incorrect. This is the change in $f(x)$ between rows. It ignores that $x$ steps by $6$, not $1$.

Choice D is incorrect. This is $f(4)$, the first row of the table. The table does not start at $x=0$.

**Desmos check:** Enter the table as $x_1$, $y_1$ and type $y_1 \sim mx_1+b$; Desmos gives $m=2.5$ and $b=12$, so $f(0)=12$.

distractor_notes.A: Gave the slope $2.5$ (kilometers per centimeter) instead of the value of $f(0)$.
distractor_notes.C: Took the change in $f(x)$ between rows, $15$, ignoring that $x$ increases by $6$ per row.
distractor_notes.D: Used the first table row, $f(4)=22$, as if it were the value at $x=0$.

stem:
A biologist models the number of bacteria in a culture $t$ hours after the start of an experiment with the function $B(t) = a \cdot b^{t}$, where $a$ and $b$ are positive constants. The table shows three values of $B(t)$.

| $t$ (hours) | $B(t)$ |
|:---:|:---:|
| 2 | 720 |
| 4 | 1,620 |
| 6 | 3,645 |

According to the model, how many bacteria were in the culture at the start of the experiment, when $t = 0$?
explanation:
The correct answer is 320.

The value of $t$ goes up by 2 each row, not by 1. From one row to the next, $B(t)$ is multiplied by $\frac{1{,}620}{720} = 2.25$. Check the next pair: $\frac{3{,}645}{1{,}620} = 2.25$. So every 2 hours the count is multiplied by 2.25, which means $b^2 = 2.25$ and $b = 1.5$.

Circle what the question asks for: the count at $t = 0$, which is $a$. Go back 2 hours from $t = 2$: $a = \frac{720}{2.25} = 320$. You can also solve $a(1.5)^2 = 720$, which gives $2.25a = 720$, so $a = 320$.

Check: $320(1.5)^4 = 320(5.0625) = 1{,}620$. ✓

Likely wrong answers:
- 720 is the first row of the table. That row is at $t = 2$, not $t = 0$.
- 480 comes from dividing 720 by 1.5 only once. That goes back just 1 hour, to $t = 1$.
- About 142.2 comes from treating 2.25 as the hourly factor and dividing 720 by $2.25^2$.
- $-180$ comes from treating the data as linear (adding 900 per row) and subtracting 900 from 720.

**Desmos check:** Enter the table as $t_1$ and $y_1$, then type $y_1 \sim a \cdot b^{t_1}$; the regression gives $a = 320$ and $b = 1.5$.

distractor_notes.480: Divided 720 by the hourly factor 1.5 only once, which goes back to t = 1 instead of t = 0.
distractor_notes.720: Used the first table row as the starting value; that row is at t = 2, not t = 0.
distractor_notes.142.2: Took the row-to-row factor 2.25 as the hourly factor b and divided 720 by 2.25 squared.
distractor_notes.-180: Treated the table as linear with a change of 900 per row and subtracted 900 from 720.

stem:
A company sells a set of nesting storage boxes. The boxes are numbered 1, 2, 3, and so on, from largest to smallest, and all the boxes are similar rectangular boxes. The volume of box $n$, in cubic centimeters, is given by the function $V$ defined by $V(n) = a\cdot b^{n}$, where $a$ and $b$ are positive constants. The table shows the volumes of four of the boxes.

| $n$ | $V(n)$ |
|:---:|:---:|
| 2 | 3,072 |
| 4 | 384 |
| 6 | 48 |
| 8 | 6 |

Each edge of box $n+1$ is $k$ times the length of the corresponding edge of box $n$, where $k$ is a constant. What is the value of $k$?
explanation:
Choice D is correct. Circle what the question asks for: an edge-length factor for one box to the next, not the volume factor $b$.

In the table, $n$ goes up by 2 in each row, and the volume is multiplied by $\frac{384}{3{,}072} = \frac{1}{8}$ each time. So $b^2 = \frac{1}{8}$, and since $b > 0$, $b = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}$. This is the volume factor from one box to the next.

The boxes are similar, so if every edge is multiplied by $k$, the volume is multiplied by $k^3$. So $k^3 = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4} = 2^{-3/2}$, which gives $k = 2^{-1/2} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$.

Check by a second route: over two boxes the volume factor is $k^6 = \frac{1}{8}$, so $k^2 = \frac{1}{2}$ and $k = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$.

Choice A is incorrect. This is the volume factor from one row of the table to the next. It covers two boxes, and it is for volume, not edge length.

Choice B is incorrect. This is $b$, the volume factor from one box to the next. It still needs a cube root to become an edge-length factor.

Choice C is incorrect. This is the edge-length factor over two boxes. It comes from taking the cube root of $\frac{1}{8}$ and ignoring that $n$ steps by 2.

**Desmos check:** Enter the table as $x_1, y_1$, run $y_1 \sim a\cdot b^{x_1}$ to get $b \approx 0.35355$, then type $b^{1/3}$ to get $0.70711 \approx \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$.

distractor_notes.A: Used the row-to-row volume ratio $\frac{1}{8}$ directly. This ignores both the step of 2 in $n$ and the cube relationship between volume and edge length.
distractor_notes.B: Found $b = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}$ correctly but gave the volume factor as the answer. Forgot that for similar solids the volume factor is $k^3$.
distractor_notes.C: Took the cube root of the row ratio $\frac{1}{8}$ to get $\frac{1}{2}$. Treated each row as one box and ignored that $n$ steps by 2.

stem: A delivery company assigns packages to two routes that each have $x$ stops. The expression $5(x+2)-2(x+3)$ gives how many more packages are on Route A than on Route B. This expression is equivalent to $ax+b$ for all values of $x$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants. What is the value of $a$?
explanation:
Choice A is correct. Distribute: $5(x+2)=5x+10$ and $-2(x+3)=-2x-6$. Combine like terms: $5x-2x+10-6=3x+4$. Matching $3x+4$ to $ax+b$ gives $a=3$ and $b=4$. Circle what the question asks for: it asks for $a$, so the answer is $3$.

Choice B is incorrect. This is $b$, the constant term, not the coefficient of $x$.

Choice C is incorrect. This comes from a sign error: distributing $-2$ as $+2x$, which gives $5x+2x=7x$.

Choice D is incorrect. This is the product $ab=3\cdot4$, not $a$.

**Desmos check:** Make a table with x₁ values 0, 1, 2, 3 and y₁ = 5(x₁+2) − 2(x₁+3), then type y₁ ~ a x₁ + b; Desmos returns a = 3 and b = 4.

distractor_notes.B: Gives b, the constant term (10 − 6 = 4), instead of a.
distractor_notes.C: Sign error: distributes −2 as +2x, so 5x + 2x = 7x.
distractor_notes.D: Multiplies a and b (3 × 4 = 12) instead of giving a alone.

topic: packages on two delivery routes

stem:
$$(ax+5)(x+c)=3x^2-7x-20$$

In the equation above, $a$ and $c$ are constants. If the equation is true for all values of $x$, what is the value of $ac$?
explanation:
Choice A is correct. Expand the left side: $(ax+5)(x+c)=ax^2+(ac+5)x+5c$. Since the equation is true for all $x$, the matching coefficients must be equal.

- $x^2$ terms: $a=3$.
- Constant terms: $5c=-20$, so $c=-4$.
- Check the $x$ terms: $ac+5=(3)(-4)+5=-7$, which matches.

Circle what the question asks for: $ac=(3)(-4)=-12$.

Choice B is incorrect. This is the value of $c$, not the value of $ac$.

Choice C is incorrect. This is the sum $a+c=3+(-4)$, not the product $ac$.

Choice D is incorrect. This comes from a sign error: solving $5c=-20$ as $c=4$ gives $ac=12$.

**Desmos check:** Make a table with $x_1$ = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and $y_1=3x_1^2-7x_1-20$, then type $y_1\sim(ax_1+5)(x_1+c)$; Desmos returns $a=3$, $c=-4$, so $ac=-12$.

distractor_notes.B: Gives the value of $c$, $-4$, instead of the product $ac$.
distractor_notes.C: Gives the sum $a+c=3+(-4)=-1$ instead of the product.
distractor_notes.D: Sign error: takes $c=4$ from $5c=-20$, so $ac=12$.

topic: quadratic identity, product of constants

stem:
A museum estimates that when a new gallery contains $x$ interactive exhibits, its visitors spend an average of $\frac{54x+33}{3x+2}$ minutes in the gallery. The equation

$$\frac{54x+33}{3x+2}=a+\frac{b}{x+c}$$

is true for all $x \ge 0$, where $a$, $b$, and $c$ are constants. What is the value of $abc$?
explanation:
The correct answer is $-12$.

**Step 1: Divide.** Since $18(3x+2)=54x+36$, the numerator is $54x+33=18(3x+2)-3$. That gives
$$\frac{54x+33}{3x+2}=18-\frac{3}{3x+2}.$$

**Step 2: Match the form.** The target form has $x+c$ in the denominator, so the coefficient of $x$ must be 1. Divide the top and bottom of the fraction by 3:
$$-\frac{3}{3x+2}=\frac{-1}{x+\frac{2}{3}}.$$
So $a=18$, $b=-1$ and $c=\frac{2}{3}$.

**Step 3: Circle what the question asks for.** It asks for the product: $abc=18(-1)\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)=-12$.

**Check:** At $x=0$ the original expression is $\frac{33}{2}=16.5$, and $18+\frac{-1}{2/3}=18-1.5=16.5$. At $x=1$ the original is $\frac{87}{5}=17.4$, and $18-\frac{1}{5/3}=18-0.6=17.4$.

Likely wrong answers:
- $-108$ comes from reading $b=-3$ and $c=2$ straight off $18-\frac{3}{3x+2}$. That ignores the fact that the denominator must be $x+c$.
- $-36$ comes from rescaling only part of the fraction, for example $b=-3$ with $c=\frac{2}{3}$.
- $12$ is a sign error, such as taking $c=-\frac{2}{3}$ by reading the form as $x-c$, or taking $b=1$.
- $\frac{53}{3}$ is $a+b+c$, the sum instead of the product.

**Desmos check:** Enter x₁ = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 in a table with y₁ = (54x₁+33)/(3x₁+2), regress y₁ ~ a + b/(x₁ + c) to get a = 18, b = −1, c ≈ 0.6667, then compute abc = −12.

distractor_notes.12: Sign error: used c = −2/3 (reading the form as x − c) or b = +1.
distractor_notes.-108: Took b = −3 and c = 2 directly from 18 − 3/(3x+2) without making the coefficient of x equal to 1.
distractor_notes.-36: Rescaled only one part of the fraction: b = −3 with c = 2/3, or b = −1 with c = 2.
distractor_notes.53/3: Found a + b + c = 18 − 1 + 2/3 instead of the product abc.

stem: In a clinical trial of an experimental medication, the concentration of the medication in a participant's bloodstream $t$ hours after a single dose is modeled by the function $C(t) = a(b)^t$, where $C(t)$ is measured in milligrams per liter and $a$ and $b$ are positive constants. According to the model, the concentration was $200$ milligrams per liter at $t = 0$ and $50$ milligrams per liter at $t = 2$. What is the value of $b$?
explanation:
The correct answer is $\frac{1}{2}$.

Circle what the question asks for: the base $b$, not the starting value.

At $t = 0$, $b^0 = 1$, so $C(0) = a = 200$.

At $t = 2$: $200b^2 = 50$, so $b^2 = \frac{1}{4}$. Because $b$ is positive, $b = \frac{1}{2}$.

Check: $C(2) = 200\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = 200 \cdot \frac{1}{4} = 50$. This matches.

- $200$ is incorrect. This is $a$, the value of $C(0)$, not $b$.
- $\frac{1}{4}$ (or $0.25$) is incorrect. This is $b^2$, the factor over two hours, not the factor for one hour.
- $4$ is incorrect. This is $\frac{200}{50}$, the ratio taken the wrong way round, and it is still for two hours.
- $150$ or $75$ is incorrect. These come from treating the drop as linear instead of exponential.

**Desmos check:** Enter lists $x_1 = [0, 2]$ and $y_1 = [200, 50]$, then regress $y_1 \sim a b^{x_1}$; Desmos returns $a = 200$ and $b = 0.5$.

distractor_notes.4: Divided $200$ by $50$, which inverts the ratio, and also skipped the square root.
distractor_notes.75: Treated the decrease as linear: $(200 - 50) \div 2 = 75$ milligrams per liter per hour.
distractor_notes.200: Gave the constant $a$ (which equals $C(0)$) instead of $b$.
distractor_notes.1/4: Found $b^2 = \frac{50}{200}$ and forgot to take the square root, so this is the two-hour factor.

topic: drug concentration decay in a clinical trial

stem: A town council conducted a series of polls of town residents after a new community garden opened. The estimated number of residents who had heard about the garden $t$ weeks after it opened is modeled by the function $N(t) = a \cdot b^t$, where $a$ and $b$ are positive constants. The model estimates that 180 residents had heard about the garden 2 weeks after it opened and 405 residents had heard about it 4 weeks after it opened. What is the value of $a$?
explanation:
Choice A is correct. Substitute both points into the model: $ab^2 = 180$ and $ab^4 = 405$. Divide the second equation by the first: $b^2 = \frac{405}{180} = 2.25$, so $b = 1.5$ (since $b$ is positive). Then $a(2.25) = 180$, so $a = \frac{180}{2.25} = 80$. Check: $80(1.5)^4 = 80(5.0625) = 405$.

Choice B is incorrect. This divides 180 by $b = 1.5$ only once, as if 180 were the value at $t = 1$ instead of $t = 2$.

Choice C is incorrect. This is $N(2)$, the model's value 2 weeks after the opening, not the constant $a$, which is the value at $t = 0$.

Choice D is incorrect. This multiplies 180 by $b = 1.5$ instead of dividing, which moves forward in time instead of back toward $t = 0$.

**Desmos check:** Enter $x_1 = [2, 4]$ and $y_1 = [180, 405]$ in a table, then type $y_1 \sim a \cdot b^{x_1}$; the regression gives $a = 80$ and $b = 1.5$.

distractor_notes.B: Divided 180 by b = 1.5 only once, treating the point as t = 1 instead of t = 2.
distractor_notes.C: Gave the model's value at t = 2, a given point, instead of the constant a (the value at t = 0).
distractor_notes.D: Multiplied 180 by b = 1.5 instead of dividing, moving forward in time rather than back to t = 0.

stem:
A wireless carrier tested a phone plan with three different monthly data limits. The table shows the carrier's monthly profit $P$, in thousands of dollars, for each data limit $x$, in gigabytes.

| Data limit, $x$ (gigabytes) | Monthly profit, $P$ (thousands of dollars) |
|---|---|
| 1 | 58 |
| 5 | 82 |
| 15 | 72 |

The carrier models this relationship with the function $P$ defined by $P(x) = a(x - h)^2 + k$, where $a$, $h$, and $k$ are constants. The model fits all three values in the table exactly. According to the model, a data limit of 12 gigabytes and a data limit of $c$ gigabytes, where $c \neq 12$, yield the same monthly profit. What is the value of $c$?
explanation:
Choice B is correct. Circle what the question asks for. It wants $c$, the other data limit that gives the same profit as 12 gigabytes. It does not want the vertex.

First find $h$. In Desmos, put the table into lists and regress $y_1 \sim a(x_1 - h)^2 + k$. This gives $a = -\frac{1}{2}$, $h = 9$, and $k = 90$.

By hand, write the model as $P(x) = px^2 + qx + r$ and use the three points:

- $p + q + r = 58$
- $25p + 5q + r = 82$
- $225p + 15q + r = 72$

Subtracting gives $6p + q = 6$ and $20p + q = -1$. So $p = -\frac{1}{2}$ and $q = 9$. The vertex is at $h = -\frac{q}{2p} = 9$.

A parabola is symmetric about the line $x = h$. A limit of 12 is 3 units to the right of 9, so the matching limit is 3 units to the left: $c = 9 - 3 = 6$.

Check: $P(6) = -\frac{1}{2}(6-9)^2 + 90 = 85.5$ and $P(12) = -\frac{1}{2}(12-9)^2 + 90 = 85.5$.

Choice A is incorrect. This assumes the axis of symmetry is halfway between 1 and 15, at $x = 8$. That only works if $P(1) = P(15)$, but $58 \neq 72$.

Choice C is incorrect. This is $h$, the data limit that gives the maximum profit, not the other limit with the same profit as 12 gigabytes.

Choice D is incorrect. This is $2h$, the sum of the two limits ($c + 12$). The 12 still has to be subtracted.

**Desmos check:** Enter x1: 1, 5, 15 and y1: 58, 82, 72, then type y1 ~ a(x1 − h)^2 + k to get a = −0.5, h = 9, k = 90. Graph y = −0.5(x − 9)^2 + 90 with y = 85.5; the intersections are at x = 6 and x = 12.

distractor_notes.A: Uses only the two outer points as if they had equal profits. This puts the axis at x = 8 and reflects 12 to get 4, but P(1) = 58 and P(15) = 72 are not equal.
distractor_notes.C: Stops at the constant h = 9, the data limit with the greatest profit, instead of reflecting 12 across x = 9.
distractor_notes.D: Finds the sum of the two equal-profit limits, 2h = 18 (the coefficient in x^2 − 18x + 72 = 0), and forgets to subtract 12.

stem:
In playwright Tomasz Wierzbicki's comedy *Flour and Feud*, two bakers on the same village street spend the first act secretly sabotaging each other's ovens. The tone shifts in the second ______ a sudden flood forces the bitter rivals to share a single kitchen.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
Choice A is correct. "The tone shifts in the second act" is a complete sentence, and "a sudden flood forces the bitter rivals to share a single kitchen" is also a complete sentence. Two complete sentences can be joined with a semicolon. Trust the Split Test, not your ear.

Choice B is incorrect. A comma alone cannot join two complete sentences; this creates a comma splice.

Choice C is incorrect. With no punctuation, the two complete sentences run together, creating a run-on sentence.

Choice D is incorrect. "Then" is not a FANBOYS conjunction, so a comma plus "then" still creates a comma splice.

distractor_notes.B: Comma splice: joins two independent clauses with only a comma.
distractor_notes.C: Run-on: no punctuation between two independent clauses.
distractor_notes.D: Comma + fake joiner: treats "then" as if it were a coordinating conjunction.

stem:
In 1845, textile workers in Lowell, Massachusetts, formed the Lowell Female Labor Reform Association to campaign for a ten-hour workday. Led by mill worker Sarah Bagley, the group gathered thousands of signatures on petitions to the state legislature ______ these petitions prompted lawmakers to hold public hearings on conditions in the state's factories.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
Choice D is correct. Use the Split Test. "Led by mill worker Sarah Bagley, the group gathered thousands of signatures on petitions to the state legislature" is a complete sentence. "These petitions prompted lawmakers to hold public hearings on conditions in the state's factories" is also a complete sentence. Two complete sentences can be joined with a semicolon, so choice D is correct.

Choice A is incorrect. With no punctuation, the two complete sentences run together, creating a run-on sentence.

Choice B is incorrect. A comma alone cannot join two complete sentences. This creates a comma splice.

Choice C is incorrect. "Then" is not a FANBOYS conjunction, so a comma plus "then" is still a comma splice.

distractor_notes.A: No punctuation between two independent clauses (run-on).
distractor_notes.B: Comma alone between two independent clauses (comma splice).
distractor_notes.C: Comma plus the fake joiner "then," which is not a coordinating conjunction (still a comma splice).

stem:
Elephants use more than loud trumpets to stay in touch. Their low-frequency rumbles, which often include tones too deep for human ears to detect______ can carry for several kilometers, letting separated members of a family group keep track of one another.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
Choice D is correct. The clause "which often include tones too deep for human ears to detect" is extra information about the rumbles. It opens with a comma after "rumbles," so it must close with a comma too. Removal test: "Their low-frequency rumbles can carry for several kilometers" is a complete sentence, so the element is nonessential and needs a matching pair of commas.

Choice A is incorrect. A semicolon must join two independent clauses. Here it would split the subject "rumbles" from its verb "can carry."

Choice B is incorrect. The extra information opens with a comma, so it can't close with a dash. The marks must match.

Choice C is incorrect. With no closing mark, the nonessential clause runs straight into the main verb "can carry," and the opening comma is left without its partner.

distractor_notes.A: Uses a semicolon, which separates the subject "rumbles" from its verb "can carry"; no independent clause precedes it.
distractor_notes.B: Mismatched marks: the element opens with a comma but closes with a dash.
distractor_notes.C: Omits the closing comma, leaving the nonessential clause unclosed.

Only after weeks of revision does she invite her company to test the patterns.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:

It opens with a comma after "sketches," so it must close with a comma too. Removal test: "Her early sketches map each dancer's path across the stage..." is a complete sentence, which shows the phrase is nonessential and needs matching commas.

Choice A is incorrect. A semicolon must join two independent clauses. Here it would cut the subject "Her early sketches" off from its verb "map."

Choice C is incorrect. The extra information opens with a comma, so it cannot close with a dash. The marks must match.

Choice D is incorrect. With no closing mark, the nonessential phrase runs straight into the verb "map" and is never set off from the main sentence.

distractor_notes.A: Uses a semicolon, which wrongly separates the subject "Her early sketches" from its verb "map"; what follows is not an independent clause.

stem:
Hydrothermal vents on the deep seafloor release water heated by underlying magma. Although sunlight never reaches these sites, the vents support a surprising variety of ______ giant tube worms, pale white crabs, and dense mats of bacteria.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
Choice B is correct. The words before the blank form a complete sentence: "the vents support a surprising variety of life." What follows is a list that names the kinds of life. A colon is the right mark to introduce a list after a complete sentence.

Choice A is incorrect. A comma makes "life" read as the first item in the list, as if "life" were one more thing alongside the tube worms, crabs, and bacteria. It does not signal that the list explains what "life" means.

Choice C is incorrect. A semicolon must join two complete sentences, and "giant tube worms, pale white crabs, and dense mats of bacteria" is not a complete sentence.

Choice D is incorrect. With no punctuation, "life" runs straight into "giant tube worms," so the sentence never marks where the list begins.

distractor_notes.A: Uses a comma to introduce the list, which makes "life" look like a separate list item instead of the word the list explains.
distractor_notes.C: Uses a semicolon, which needs a complete sentence on both sides; the list after the blank is not a sentence.
distractor_notes.D: Leaves out punctuation, running the complete sentence directly into the list.
